instrument.title: Impedance Feedback
instrument.subtitle: As target cells lyse, released intracellular ions shift medium conductivity σ_e, modelled via the Maxwell-Garnett mixing rule. The cuvette impedance is computed at the actual broadcast frequency, not just DC. For RF sources (50 Ω), impedance mismatch and power delivery efficiency are tracked. A voltage-divider correction keeps the delivered field at the set point despite conductivity drift.

view.calloutIonNote: Maxwell-Garnett mixing rule · φ = φ_cells × f_lysed · valid for both high-σ and low-σ media
view.calloutZNote: DC model (f ≪ 365 MHz) · full complex ∣Z(f)∣ computed at broadcast frequency in the panel below
view.pocBody: In simulated mode, impedance drift is computed from the ion-release physics model (cell volume fraction × lysed fraction × σ contrast). Switch to Live Hardware in the Hardware Input panel to replace this with real measurements from a lab impedance analyser or LCR meter connected via the impedanceReading socket event. See the Protocol page for the full hardware integration specification.
view.tipContextTarget: Target Cell Currently selected target cell type. The impedance model uses its radius and intracellular conductivity to compute ion release on lysis.
view.tipContextDR: Disruption Ratio (target) DR = (V_m · PEF) / V_threshold. Values above 85% indicate the lysis window has been reached.
view.tipContextCorrection: Voltage Correction Factor = 1 + R_s / Z_cuvette Values above 1 mean the generator must output proportionally more voltage to compensate for impedance drift.
view.tipContextJoule: Medium Joule Heating Power [mW] P = |E|² × σ_e × V_cuvette Total power dissipated as heat in the medium between the electrodes. Higher σ_e (post-lysis) and higher field → more heating. Corresponding adiabatic temperature rise rate: dT/dt = |E|² × σ_e / (ρ × c_p) This is an upper bound, actual rise is lower due to heat loss to cuvette walls.

setup.title: Cuvette Setup
setup.sub: Electrode geometry · source impedance · cell seeding density
setup.gapSub: Distance between electrodes [mm], defines E = V/d
setup.areaSub: Electrode face area [cm²], with gap, sets cuvette resistance Z = d/(σ·A)
setup.sourceRSub: Generator + cable impedance [Ω], typically 50 Ω for RF, variable for pulsed
setup.densitySub: Target cell seeding density [cells/mL], sets ion release magnitude on lysis
setup.tipPreset: Cuvette Preset Standard electroporation cuvette geometries from BTX and Bio-Rad. Gap sets E = V/d; area sets impedance Z = d/(σ·A). Use 'Custom' to enter arbitrary geometry.
setup.tipGap: Electrode Gap [mm] Determines the electric field: E = V_applied / d. Smaller gap → higher field per volt, but lower cuvette impedance. Typical lab cuvettes: 1 mm, 2 mm, 4 mm.
setup.tipArea: Electrode Cross-Section [cm²] With gap, sets cuvette DC resistance: Z = d / (σ_e × A). BTX cuvettes ≈ 0.10 cm²; Bio-Rad ≈ 0.13 cm².
setup.tipSourceR: Source Impedance R_s [Ω] Generator output + cable impedance. 50 Ω, standard RF / coaxial system < 1 Ω, typical high-voltage pulsed power unit Higher R_s → larger voltage-divider correction needed.
setup.tipDensity: Cell Density [cells/mL] Sets the volume fraction φ = N × (4/3)π R³. Higher density → more ions released per unit volume → larger σ_e rise on lysis. Typical: 10⁶ cells/mL mammalian, 10⁸ cells/mL bacteria.

meter.title: Live Impedance Status
meter.tipNominal: DC Nominal Impedance Z₀ [Ω] Computed at experiment start with fresh medium and no lysis: Z_DC = d / (σ_e_base × A) DC limit, capacitive term negligible for f ≪ f_relax. Used as reference for drift percentage.
meter.tipZAtFreq: |Z(f)| at {freq} [Ω] Complex impedance magnitude at the current broadcast frequency. |Z(f)| = (d/A) / √[σ_e² + (ωε_rε₀)²] DC approximation Z₀ = {zDC} Ω · |Z(f)| = {zF} Ω Maxwell relaxation frequency: f_relax ≈ {relax} MHz Above f_relax the capacitive term dominates and |Z| falls rapidly.
meter.tipDrift: Impedance Drift [%] (Z_current − Z_nominal) / Z_nominal × 100 Negative = impedance fell (σ_e rose from ion release). A −10% drift requires a +11% field correction.
meter.tipSigmaBase: Base Medium Conductivity σ_e [S/m] Nominal conductivity of the selected medium at 37°C. This is the experiment starting point before any cells lyse.
meter.tipSigmaLive: Live σ_e [S/m] Effective medium conductivity after Maxwell-Garnett ion-release correction. σ_eff = σ_m × [σ_i + 2σ_m + 2φ(σ_i−σ_m)] / [σ_i + 2σ_m − φ(σ_i−σ_m)] φ = φ_cells × f_lysed · Handles both σ_i > σ_m and σ_i < σ_m media.
meter.tipRelax: Maxwell Relaxation Frequency [MHz] f_relax = σ_e / (2π ε_r ε₀) Below this frequency the medium behaves resistively (DC model valid). Above it, capacitive displacement currents become significant and the DC impedance formula Z = d/(σ·A) under-estimates the true |Z(f)|. For saline (σ=1.5 S/m, εr=74): f_relax ≈ 365 MHz.
meter.tipFieldDistortion: Electric Field Distortion at φ = {phi}% Field enhancement factor: E_local / E_applied = (1 + φ/2) / (1 − φ) = {factor} At high cell density, intact cells (insulating membranes) force current through narrowing extracellular channels, concentrating the field at cell surfaces. The Schwan equation uses E_applied, the actual membrane potential is E_local × 1.5R×cosθ / √(1+(ωτ)²), which is {factor}× higher than displayed. Level: {level}, negligible below φ=1%, significant above φ=5%.

bode.title: ∣Z(f)∣ Frequency Response
bode.sub: Cuvette impedance magnitude vs frequency, log-log scale

corrector.title: Field Correction
corrector.sub: Generator output needed to maintain target transmembrane voltage
corrector.tipTarget: Target Field [V/cm] The electric field required inside the cuvette to achieve the desired transmembrane voltage. Set in the Experiment Lab Field Control slider.
corrector.tipCorrected: Corrected Generator Field [V/cm] The equivalent field the generator must output to deliver E_target inside the cuvette after accounting for the voltage divider: E_gen = E_target × (1 + R_s / Z_cuvette) Set this value on your function generator or pulser.
corrector.tipFactor: Voltage Correction Factor = 1 + R_s / Z_cuvette Multiply nominal generator voltage by this factor to compensate for impedance drift.
corrector.tipVSWR: VSWR & Power Delivery (RF mode) Reflection coefficient: Γ = |Z_load − Z₀| / |Z_load + Z₀| = {gamma} VSWR = (1 + |Γ|) / (1 − |Γ|) = {vswr} Power delivery η = 1 − |Γ|² = {efficiency} Z_load = {zLoad} Ω · Z₀ = {z0} Ω VSWR ≤ 2.0 is standard practice (η ≥ 88.9%). Note: VSWR only matters for RF (50 Ω) sources; IRE pulsers (<1 Ω source) are effectively matched to any biological load.
corrector.tipSourceNote: Source Impedance R_s [Ω] IRE pulsers (R_s < 1 Ω): Source ≪ Z_load, voltage divider is negligible; VSWR mismatch analysis does not apply. RF generators (R_s = 50 Ω): Source and load are comparable, field correction and VSWR are critical. At 50 Ω with a saline cuvette (Z ≈ 200-1000 Ω), typical Γ ≈ 0.6, η ≈ 64%. Impedance matching networks improve delivery.
corrector.rcStatus_ok: Cuvette RC bandwidth OK, full field delivered
corrector.rcStatus_marginal: Pulse shorter than 5×τ_RC, partial field attenuation
corrector.rcStatus_critical: Pulse shorter than τ_RC, severe field attenuation
corrector.tipRCBandwidth: Cuvette RC Bandwidth Check τ_RC = ε_r × ε₀ / σ_e = {tau} ns (geometry-independent) t_p = {tp} ns · ratio t_p/τ_RC = {ratio} The medium acts as an RC circuit with time constant τ_RC. Pulses shorter than τ_RC cannot fully charge the cuvette, the delivered field is attenuated before reaching steady state. Rule of thumb: t_p > 5×τ_RC → full field (≥99% of set value) t_p = 1×τ_RC → 63% field delivery t_p < τ_RC → severe attenuation σ_e = {sigma} S/m at this moment.

hardware.title: Hardware Input
hardware.sub: Connect a lab impedance analyser to override the simulated model
hardware.schemaNote: Send JSON to the socket event 'impedanceReading' from your instrument bridge. All numeric fields use SI units.
hardware.tipMode: Sensor Mode Simulated, impedance is computed from the ion-release physics model based on the current disruption ratio. Live Hardware, the simulated value is replaced by Z_real from the last instrument packet. Switch to Live Hardware only after confirming your instrument bridge is sending readings.
hardware.tipSocket: Socket Event: impedanceReading Your instrument bridge should emit this event to the ResoPulse backend socket. The backend validates and re-broadcasts to all connected UI clients. Minimal schema: zReal: number (Ω, required) zImag: number (Ω, required) freqHz: number (Hz, required) timestamp: number (Unix ms, required) conductivity?: number (S/m, optional)

trend.title: Impedance Trend
trend.sub: Historical Z readings, simulated (grey) or hardware (cyan)
trend.noData: No history yet, readings will appear as cells lyse or hardware data arrives

loadMonitor.title: Load Impedance Monitor
loadMonitor.sub: Continuous σ_e and Z tracking, 1 s auto-sampling, 2-minute rolling window
loadMonitor.tipMediumSAR: Medium Joule Heating SAR [W/kg] SAR_medium = σ_e × E²_rms / ρ_water This is the dominant heating source at low cell packing fractions (φ < 0.1). A thermocouple placed in the cuvette measures this medium heating, not the cell SAR. For protocol calibration, compare medium SAR with cell SAR to understand the total thermal load. At high duty cycles (CW or dc > 0.01), medium heating can cause bulk temperature rises that alter σ_e and shift the electroporation threshold. Ref: Foster & Schwan (1989); standard Joule heating formula.
loadMonitor.noData: Collecting data: chart appears after 3 samples (~3 s)
loadMonitor.tipState: Load State Based on absolute impedance drift from nominal. Nominal: |ΔZ| < 5%, no correction needed Warning: 5-15%, minor correction recommended Critical: >15%, significant drift; apply corrected field
loadMonitor.tipSigmaBase: Base Medium Conductivity σ_e [S/m] Nominal conductivity of the selected medium at 37°C. This is the experiment starting point before any cells lyse.
loadMonitor.tipSigmaLive: Live Medium Conductivity σ_e [S/m] Current conductivity after accounting for ion release from lysed cells. Rises (low-σ media) or falls (high-σ media like saline) depending on the σ_i vs σ_e contrast.
loadMonitor.tipDelta: Conductivity Change Δσ_e [S/m] δσ_e = σ_e_live − σ_e_base (after Maxwell-Garnett correction) Positive: σ_i > σ_m → lysis raises conductivity (PBS, sucrose media) Negative: σ_i < σ_m → lysis lowers conductivity (saline) MG formula: σ_eff = σ_m × [σ_i + 2σ_m + 2φ_lys(σ_i−σ_m)] / [σ_i + 2σ_m − φ_lys(σ_i−σ_m)]
loadMonitor.tipDrift: Impedance Drift [%] (Z_live − Z_nominal) / Z_nominal × 100 Negative drift (saline): σ_e rises → Z falls → field under-delivered Positive drift (PBS): σ_e falls → Z rises → field over-delivered
loadMonitor.tipChain: Lysis Feedback Chain The causal sequence connecting lysis events to generator correction: f_lysed, fraction of target cells lysed (DR ≥ 85%) Δσ_e , conductivity shift from ion release ΔZ % , resulting cuvette impedance drift E_gen ×, voltage correction factor to maintain target transmembrane Vm At high cell density or long exposure, this correction can exceed 20%.

bridgeModal.title: Instrument Bridge Setup
bridgeModal.subtitle: Connect a physical impedance analyser or LCR meter to stream live Z readings into the UI

quick.title: Quick Start — Verify the full pipeline with no hardware
quick.sub: Run these steps first. Takes about 2 minutes. Confirms the bridge, backend, and UI are all communicating before connecting real equipment.
quick.s1Note: Open a terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). You should see Python 3.12.x or later.
quick.s2Note: Run from the instrument-bridge folder inside the project directory.
quick.s3Note: Starts an in-process mock Socket.IO server and validates 36 packet assertions. No hardware or running backend needed. Should print: 36/36 assertions passed.
quick.s4Note: Run from the backend folder. Keep this terminal open throughout the experiment.
quick.s5Label: Start the bridge in demo mode
quick.s5Note: Sends synthetic saline-cuvette impedance readings every second. No instrument required.
quick.s6Label: Enable Live Hardware in this panel
quick.s6Note: Click the Live Hardware button above. The status dot should turn green within 2 seconds. If it does, the full pipeline is working correctly.

btx.title: BTX ECM 830 / ECM 2001 — RS-232 Serial
btx.sub: Reads post-pulse cuvette resistance after each electroporation pulse. Requires a USB-to-serial adapter if your computer has no DB9 port.
btx.s1Label: Connect the RS-232 cable and discover the port
btx.s1Note: The probe command lists all serial ports detected on this machine. Use the port name shown (e.g. COM4 on Windows, /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux).
btx.s3Label: Start the bridge (replace COM4 with your port)
btx.s3Note: Readings arrive after at least one pulse has been triggered on the ECM. The bridge sends a status query each poll interval and parses the resistance response.
btx.warn: The BTX ECM RS-232 protocol is not publicly documented by Harvard Apparatus. The driver uses a best-effort parser based on community captures. If readings do not appear, run with --log-level DEBUG to inspect the raw serial lines, then adjust the driver if your firmware uses a different response format.

visa.title: VISA-Compatible LCR Meter — GPIB, USB, or LAN
visa.sub: Tested with Keysight E4980A, Hioki IM3533, Agilent 4284A. Any instrument that responds to standard SCPI commands (IEEE 488.2) should work.
visa.s1Note: Choose one option: NI-VISA (download from ni.com/visa, free account required), or Keysight IO Libraries (keysight.com/iosuite). For USB and LAN instruments, pyvisa-py is already included and works without installing NI-VISA on most systems.
visa.s2Label: Install VISA Python bindings and discover your resource string
visa.s2Note: The probe command lists all VISA resources detected on this machine. Copy the resource string for your instrument.
visa.s3Label: Start the bridge (replace the resource string with your address)
visa.s3Note: The bridge configures the instrument for series-Z measurements (ZS-RS SCPI function) and triggers readings at the frequency set by BRIDGE_MEAS_FREQ_HZ in your .env file.

serial.title: Generic ASCII Serial LCR — DE-5000, Peak LCR45, BK 889B
serial.sub: For instruments that stream comma or space-delimited Z values over serial without requiring SCPI commands. The bridge reads one line per poll and parses the first numeric tokens as Z_real and Z_imag.
serial.s1Label: Set the measurement frequency on the instrument front panel
serial.s1Note: These instruments cannot be commanded remotely. Set the test frequency directly on the device, then enter the same value as BRIDGE_MEAS_FREQ_HZ in the .env file so the UI reports it correctly.
serial.s2Label: Connect and discover the serial port
serial.s2Note: DE-5000 uses 2400 baud. Most other ASCII serial LCR meters use 9600. Check your instrument manual and set BRIDGE_BAUD_RATE in .env to match.
serial.s4Label: Start the bridge (replace COM3 and 2400 with your port and baud rate)
serial.s4Note: Watch the DEBUG log output on first run to verify your instrument's line format is being parsed correctly.

sonif.note: The sounds are NOT the RF frequencies (kHz-MHz range), those are far above the audible range. This is a scientific data-monitoring technique (sonification).
sonif.tip: Auditory Display (Sonification) Maps live experiment data to audible tones via the Web Audio API. These sounds are NOT the RF frequencies (kHz-MHz), which are far above the audible range. This is a scientific monitoring technique. Mappings: Impedance drift → pitch (220 Hz-1760 Hz) Disruption ratio → volume Rev-EP window → 6 Hz tremolo modulation Lysis event → 880 Hz burst Healthy-cell warning → 110 Hz pulse Ref: Kramer et al. (1999); Walker & Kramer (2006)
